# Offer Naming — The M-A-G-I-C Formula

**Source:** *$100M Offers*, "Enhancing Your Offer: Naming" (lines ~2617–2825).
The 5th enhancer: **names re-stimulate demand and expand awareness.** "Having a Grand Slam Offer will
not make you money if no one finds out about it" (l.2621). Naming determines how well advertising
converts and how big a response outbound and organic get. Same thing, named two ways: a "Free Six-Week
Stress Release Challenge" beats a "Float Tank Center Session" (l.2623).

Anchoring idea — the **implicit-egotism effect:** "we are generally drawn to the things and people that
most resemble us" (l.2619). A name that names *them* pulls them in.

---

## Why naming matters forever — the "wrapping paper" principle (l.2625–2631)

Over time, **offers fatigue** — and **faster in local markets** (a small radius / TAM is cheaply
reached in full). The fix is **not changing the offer** — the work, services, and products stay the
same. You **rename it to refresh it** — change only the *wrapping paper*. "This one concept will get
you leads forever." *(Disclaimer, l.2627: reaching an audience once ≠ fatigue — most people don't even
notice an offer on first mention; fatigue is a matter of years, not months.)*

---

## The M-A-G-I-C formula (l.2633–2645)

Five components. **Not all are mandatory — use three to five** (all five usually makes the name too
long). **Shorter and punchier is better** — a balance of brevity and specificity. **Order is
flexible** — do what sounds punchier, not strictly M-A-G-I-C. "The only way to really know what works
is to write the names out and test them" (l.2639).

Marketing theory each element maps to (l.2645):

| Letter | Component | Translates to |
|---|---|---|
| **M** | **Make a Magnetic "Reason Why"** | Attention |
| **A** | **Announce Your Avatar** | Discrimination |
| **G** | **Give Them a Goal** | Purpose |
| **I** | **Indicate a Time Interval** | Timeline |
| **C** | **Complete with a Container Word** | Method |

### M — Make a Magnetic "Reason Why" (l.2647–2659)
A word/phrase giving the "reason why" you're running the promotion. Think like a **fraternity party
planner** — the reason can be *anything* as long as you believe it (you can even make it a joke). It
should answer: *Why are they making this great offer?* and/or *Why should I respond? / What's in it
for me?*
- **Examples:** Free · 88% off · Giveaway · Spring · Summer · Back To School · Grand Opening · New
  Management · New Building · Anniversary · Halloween · New Year.

### A — Announce Your Avatar (l.2661–2665)
Call out your ideal avatar — who you *are* and *aren't* looking for. **As specific as possible, but no
more.** Locally, go **hyper-local** — the sub-market, not the city ("Not Baltimore but Towson, MD. Not
Chicago, but Hinsdale").
- **Examples:** Bee Cave Dentists · Rolling Hills Moms · Brick & Mortar Businesses · Salon Owners ·
  Retired Athletes · Brooklyn Busy Executives.

### G — Give Them a Goal (l.2667–2671)
Articulate the prospect's **dream outcome** — a word or phrase; an event, feeling, experience, or
outcome that excites them. **The more specific and tangible, the better.**
- **Examples:** Pain Free · Celebrity Smile · 1st Place · Never Out Of Breath · Perfect Product · Grand
  Slam Offer · Little Black Dress · Double Your Profit · First Client · High Ticket · 7 Figure · 100k.

### I — Indicate a Time Interval (l.2673–2681)
Tell them the **duration to expect** for results.
- **Examples:** AA Minutes · BB Hours · CC Days · DD Weeks · Z Months → "4 Hour," "21 Day," "6 Week,"
  "3 Month."
- **Compliance note (l.2679):** most ad platforms **won't approve a quantifiable claim (income/weight)
  *with* a stated duration** — it implies a guarantee. Don't pair a quantifiable outcome with a
  duration unless the platform allows it. If the goal isn't a "claim," use the interval freely:
  "$10,000 in 10 days" (risky) vs. "Make Your First Sale in 10 Days" (fine).

### C — Complete with a Container Word (l.2683–2687)
A word denoting the offer is a **bundle / system** — something that can't be held up to a commoditized
alternative.
- **Examples:** Challenge · Blueprint · Bootcamp · Intensive · Incubator · Masterclass · Program ·
  Detox · Experience · Summit · Accelerator · Fast Track · Shortcut · Sprint · Launch · Slingshot ·
  Catapult · Explosion · System · Getaway · Meetup · Transformation · Mastermind · Game Plan · Deep
  Dive · Workshop · Comeback · Rebirth · Attack · Assault · Reset · Solution · Hack · Cheatcode ·
  Liftoff.

---

## Pro Tips — make it stick

- **Find Time To Rhyme (l.2689–2695):** "Rhyme your program name to win the game." A *nice-to-have,
  not a requirement* — don't force it. (Google a rhyming dictionary.) *Examples:* Six-Pack Fast Track ·
  5-Day Book Print Sprint · Marriage Thrive Deep Dive · 12-Week 2-Putt Shortcut · 12-Month No-Debt
  Reset · Celebrity Butt Shortcut.
- **Alliteration (l.2697–2703):** most/all words start with the same sound — easier than rhyming for
  most people. Also optional; don't force it. *Examples:* Make Money Masterclass · Change Your Life
  Challenge · Big Booty Bootcamp · Debt Detox · Real Estate Reset · Life Coach Liftoff.
- **Name Sub-Items & Bonuses (l.2759–2761):** run the M-A-G-I-C formula on **each item in the stack/
  bundle** too — it automatically enhances perceived value.

## Worked name patterns by industry (l.2711–2751)
- **Wellness:** "Free Six-Week Lean-By-Halloween Challenge" · "88% Off 12-Week Bikini Blueprint" ·
  "Free 21-Day Mommy Makeover" · "60-minute Make Your Friends Jealous Model Hair System" · "(Free!)
  Bend Over Pain Free in 42 Days… Healing Fast Track."
- **Doctors:** "$2,000-Off Celebrity Smile Transformation" · "Lakeway Moms – $1,500 Off Your Kids
  Braces" · "Back to School Free Braces Giveaway" · "Back Sore No More! 90 Day Rapid Healing Intensive
  (81% off!)" · "Tightness? $1 Massage New Client Summer Special."
- **Coaching:** "5 Clients in 5 Days Blueprint" · "7F Agency 12 Week Intensive" · "14 Day Find Your
  Perfect Product Launch" · "Fill Your Gym in 30 Days (Free!)."

*(Notice each pulls 3–5 M-A-G-I-C components, not all five.)*

---

## What happens when offers fatigue — the change ladder (l.2763–2797)

As market tastes shift, vary the offer to keep lead flow steady. **Change from the top down** — the
lightest, cheapest levers first; the "machine" only as a last resort. Each step down is more
operationally heavy.

1. **Change the creative** (images/pictures in the ads).
2. **Change the body copy** in the ads.
3. **Change the headline — the "wrapper"** of your offer. *(Includes re-seasoning the name:* "Free 6
   Week Lean Challenge" → "Free 6 Week Tone Challenge"; "Holiday Hangover" → "New Year New You.")*
4. **Change the duration** of the offer (6 weeks → 28 days / 8 weeks).
5. **Change the enhancer** (the free/discount component).
6. **Change the monetization structure** — the series of offers and price points (**last resort, and
   only for a darn good reason**, especially once you have traction).

> "Once you've monetized an offer, rarely should you change it. Just rinse and repeat." (l.2789) —
> resist entrepreneurial change-for-its-own-sake; change here creates operational drag. **In a local
> market you never change the value stack — only how it *looks* to the marketplace** (l.2805).

---

## Procedure — "Name This Offer" (run this in the sub-skill)

1. **Pull the inputs** from the built offer: the **dream outcome** (→ G), the **avatar** incl.
   hyper-local sub-market if applicable (→ A), the **promotion reason** (free/discount/season/opening →
   M), the **timeframe** (→ I), and the **bundle nature** (→ C).
2. **Draft each of the 5 M-A-G-I-C slots** from those inputs (using the example word-banks above as a
   palette, not a copy source).
3. **Assemble 3–5 components** into a name — prioritize the punchiest, drop the rest to stay short.
   Reorder freely for sound (order need not be M-A-G-I-C).
4. **Apply a Pro Tip if it lands naturally** — rhyme or alliteration — but **never force it.**
5. **Run the compliance check** — if a quantifiable claim (income/weight) is paired with a duration,
   either drop the number or drop the duration for paid platforms.
6. **Generate several variants** (this is the point — "unlimited wrapping paper"). Output **2–3 best
   names** to test; note the control, then test new names against it.
7. **Optionally name each sub-item/bonus** with the same formula.
8. **Attach the fatigue ladder** so the operator knows the refresh order (creative → copy → headline/
   season → duration → enhancer → monetization) before ever touching the offer machine.

---

## Output contract for `hormozi-offer-naming`

For *this* product, produce:
1. A filled **M-A-G-I-C slot table** (M / A / G / I / C, each drawn from the product's real avatar,
   dream outcome, promo reason, and timeframe — no fabricated numbers; discounts/durations are user-set
   or `<placeholder>`).
2. **2–3 candidate names** (each using 3–5 components, punchy, reordered for sound), with rhyme/
   alliteration only where natural, and platform-compliant.
3. Optional **named sub-items/bonuses.**
4. The **fatigue-refresh ladder** as a note, so the same offer can be re-wrapped for years.
